Precondition: he points to the struct hist_entry embedded as member he of a struct kvm_event whose perf_kvm pointer is valid. Postcondition: gets the containing kvm_event with container_of, then returns percent(get_event_time(event, perf_kvm->trace_vcpu), perf_kvm->total_time) converted to int: get_event_time gives event->total.time when trace_vcpu is -1, 0 when trace_vcpu >= event->max_vcpu, otherwise event->vcpu[trace_vcpu].time; percent() computes 100.0 * st / tot in double when tot is nonzero and 0 when tot is zero; the double is truncated toward zero by the int return. No state is modified.

name: kvm_events_live_report
prose: Precondition: kvm points to an initialized perf_kvm_stat with a configured evlist. Postcondition: sets kvm->live to true, then calls cpu_isa_config; if that returns a negative value it is returned at once with no cleanup. err starts as -EINVAL. If verify_vcpu, is_valid_key or register_kvm_events_ops fails (checked before the terminal settings are saved) it jumps to the out label with err = -EINVAL. Otherwise it saves the terminal settings, initializes the histograms and installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers; if perf_kvm__timerfd_create fails it jumps to out with err = -1; if either evlist__add_pollfd or fd_set_nonblock(stdin) fails it jumps to out with err still -EINVAL. It then enables the events and loops while the done flag is clear: it calls perf_kvm__mmap_read and leaves the loop (leaving err as it was, which is -EINVAL on the first iteration or the value assigned in an earlier iteration) if that returns a negative value; it assigns err = perf_kvm__handle_timerfd (0, or -1 on a timer read error, in which case it jumps to out and skips evlist__disable and the result printing); it sets done from stdin when stdin is readable and 'q' was read; and when the mmap read returned 0 and done is clear it assigns err the return value of evlist__poll(100). After the loop it calls evlist__disable and, only if err == 0, sorts and prints the result. At out it deletes the histogram entries, closes kvm->timerfd if it is >= 0, restores the terminal settings with tcsetattr (from an uninitialized buffer if out was reached before the settings were saved), and returns err: cpu_isa_config's negative value, -EINVAL, -1, 0 (after a normal stop or an mmap-read break that follows a successful timer handling), or the last evlist__poll return value.
note: reviewer (round15) right: err=0 from perf_kvm__handle_timerfd at 1454 omitted; prose rewritten. Early-failure paths lines 1414-1441; loop 1446-1463

name: __cmd_contention
prose: Precondition: the file-scope option variables (input_name, force, use_bpf, target, filters, delays, output_fields, bpf_map_entries, max_stack_depth, stack_skip, show_* flags) are initialized; argc/argv hold the workload command line (argc may be 0). Postcondition: err starts as -EINVAL. If the calloc of lockhash_table fails it returns -ENOMEM immediately with nothing else done. Otherwise it creates a perf session (when use_bpf is set no input data is passed); if session creation fails it sets err = PTR_ERR(session) and session = NULL and goes to out_delete. In BPF mode it validates the target (a nonzero target__validate result is returned as err), installs SIGINT/SIGCHLD/SIGTERM handlers, allocates the evlist (-ENOMEM on failure), and a negative result from evlist__create_maps, evlist__prepare_workload (only when argc is nonzero) or lock_contention_prepare is returned as err. In non-BPF mode with a non-pipe input, a failing perf_session__has_traces, a missing lock:contention_begin evsel, or a failed perf_session__set_tracepoints_handlers goes to out_delete with err unchanged, i.e. -EINVAL (nothing assigns err on that path); with pipe input those checks are skipped. A nonzero result from setup_output_field or select_key is returned as err. Then in BPF mode it starts contention tracing, starts the workload if argc, blocks in pause(), stops and reads the data; otherwise it returns a nonzero result of perf_session__process_events as err. On the remaining path it calls setup_pager, sorts and prints the result and falls into out_delete with err == 0. out_delete is reached by every path after the hash table was allocated (success included): it calls lock_filter_finish, evlist__delete(con.evlist) (NULL outside BPF mode), lock_contention_finish, perf_session__delete(session), perf_env__exit and zfree(&lockhash_table), then returns err.
note: reviewer (round15) wrong: lock.c:1994 initializes err = -EINVAL and no statement on the non-BPF failure paths (2089-2103 of the file) assigns err, so the returned value is -EINVAL, as the old prose said. Old prose was imprecise elsewhere (no-trace checks only when !use_bpf && !is_pipe; the cleanup also runs on success); rewritten. Slice line numbers do not match the current file (function at 1992-2154).

name: report_lock_release_event
prose: Precondition: evsel and sample describe a lock release tracepoint event carrying the 'name' and 'lockdep_addr' fields. Postcondition: returns the negative value from get_key_by_aggr_mode_simple if it fails, and -ENOMEM if lock_stat_findnew, thread_stat_findnew or get_seq returns NULL; otherwise it returns 0 after acting on the state of the lock sequence seq: for SEQ_STATE_UNINITIALIZED nothing is changed; for SEQ_STATE_ACQUIRED it increments ls->nr_release, then unlinks seq from its list and frees it; for SEQ_STATE_READ_ACQUIRED it decrements seq->read_count (BUG_ON if that goes negative) and, if the count is still nonzero, increments ls->nr_release and keeps seq, otherwise it increments ls->nr_release and then unlinks and frees seq; for SEQ_STATE_ACQUIRING, SEQ_STATE_CONTENDED or SEQ_STATE_RELEASED (broken sequence) it sets ls->broken and increments bad_hist[BROKEN_RELEASE] only if ls->broken was clear, does not change nr_release, and unlinks and frees seq; any other state hits BUG_ON.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the ACQUIRED path also unlinks and frees seq (lock.c:819-822); the earlier reviewer's 'returns 0 without updating release counts for uninitialized/broken' was a description, not an error, and is covered by the rewrite

name: record__switch_output
prose: Precondition: rec has a valid session, evlist and data, and rec->switch_output is initialized (filenames array allocated when num_files is nonzero). Postcondition: it first waits for AIO mmap reads, calls write_finished_init(rec, true) and record__synthesize(rec, true) (and record__synthesize_workload(rec, true) when no target is set); each of these three does something only when rec->opts.tail_synthesize is true, and their return values are ignored. It then sets rec->samples to 0 and calls record__finish_output. If fetch_current_timestamp fails it prints a message and returns -EINVAL at that point, before perf_data__switch is called and before any switch_output bookkeeping. Otherwise it calls perf_data__switch (fd is its result, negative on failure); when fd >= 0 and !at_exit it resets rec->bytes_written and the session header data_size to 0; unless quiet it prints a 'Dump' line to stderr; when switch_output.num_files is nonzero it advances cur_file cyclically, removes and frees any old filename in that slot and stores new_filename there, otherwise it frees new_filename (this bookkeeping is done whether or not fd is negative). When !at_exit it then calls record__synthesize(rec, false), record__synthesize_workload(rec, false) if no target is set and write_finished_init(rec, false), each of which acts only if rec->opts.tail_synthesize is false (return values ignored). It returns fd.
note: reviewer (round15) right: write_finished_init/record__synthesize/record__synthesize_workload each return 0 immediately unless opts.tail_synthesize == tail (record.c:1861,2065,1843); prose said they happen unconditionally. Earlier reviewer's -EINVAL/negative fd points were right and kept.

name: __cmd_record
prose: Precondition: rec is a configured struct record with an evlist, options and output data; argc > 0 means a workload command in argv is to be forked. Postcondition (slice cut the head; this is the body of __cmd_record, builtin-record.c:2397-2953): it installs signal handlers and trigger state, creates the perf session and returns PTR_ERR(session) if that fails. These early checks return directly, without deleting the session or running the cleanup labels: -1 if threaded recording is requested together with pipe output or full AUX tracing, -1 if zstd_init fails, -1 if kcore copy was requested and kcore is not readable, -1 if record__init_clock fails (and -1 for cgroup tracking when HAVE_FILE_HANDLE is not defined). Failure to create or register the wakeup eventfd, or to prepare the workload, sets status (-1 or the error) and jumps to out_delete_session. A failure of record__open sets err = -1, a failing kcore copy, header write, record__setup_sb_evlist or a negative record__synthesize result keeps its nonzero or negative value as err, a missing build-id feature (without --no-buildid) sets err = -1, a failed sched_setscheduler sets err = -1, and all of these jump to out_free_threads; if record__start_threads fails it also jumps to out_free_threads but without assigning err, so err keeps the non-negative value from record__synthesize. If forking, it synthesizes COMM and NAMESPACES events (malloc failure: err = -ENOMEM and jump to out_child; perf_event__synthesize_comm returning -1 also jumps to out_child with err unchanged) and starts the workload; a failure of event_enable_timer__start or write_finished_init(rec, false) jumps to out_child with that error. The main loop (lines 2698-2827) repeats: when the switch-output trigger, done or draining is set it toggles the overwrite ring to data-pending; record__mmap_read_all failure sets both triggers to error, err = -1 and jumps to out_child_no_flush (no final flush); a failed AUX snapshot sets err = -1 and goes to out_child; a hit switch-output trigger re-reads (continue) while the overwrite ring is still running, otherwise it calls record__switch_output and a negative fd sets err = fd and goes to out_child; when no new samples were produced it breaks if done or draining, else polls the fds, filters POLLERR/POLLHUP fds (setting draining when that filter returns 0) and assigns err from record__update_evlist_pollfd_from_thread (a nonzero value goes to out_child, overwriting the poll result); it handles control-fd commands (STOP sets done), and event_enable_timer__process returning negative goes to out_child, positive sets done and err = 0; when done it disables the events once unless there is no target. After the loop it turns off the triggers, does the final BPF metadata and AUX snapshot work, and if the workload failed to exec it prints a message, sets err = -1 and goes to out_child; otherwise it writes the tail finished-init (and tail workload synthesis, when applicable). out_child stops the threads and flushes once more with record__mmap_read_all(rec, true); then out_free_threads frees thread data, finalizes the control fd and syncs AIO. For a forked workload it sends SIGTERM if the child has not finished, waits, and sets status = err when err < 0, else the child's exit code if it exited, otherwise leaves status unchanged (0) when it was killed by a signal; without a workload status = err. If err == 0 it then does the tail synthesis and finishes the output (or switches the output file when timestamp_filename is set, a negative fd going to out_delete_session with status = fd), prints the capture summary unless quiet, and at out_delete_session closes done_fd, finalizes zstd, stops the side-band thread when bpf events are enabled, deletes the session and returns status.
note: slice cut the head; real function is __cmd_record. Read full function 2397-2953. No reviewer claims in packet (dropped as unnamed). Large function, read in full.

name: cmd_record
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are the 'perf record' command line; the file-scope record struct and record_options table exist (cmd_record itself allocates rec->evlist). Postcondition (cmd_record at builtin-record.c:4069-4396): it returns -ENOMEM at once if evlist__new fails, and returns perf_config's or symbol__validate_sym_arguments' nonzero result at once; these three early returns do not delete the evlist. After option parsing, every later return passes through out_opts, which closes the control fds and deletes the evlist, or through out, which first frees the thread masks, calls symbol__exit and frees the auxtrace record and then falls into out_opts. Values returned via out_opts directly: -EINVAL for latency profiling with system-wide collection, for cgroup sampling without kernel support, for missing switch-event support, for a failed switch_output_setup, and when the calloc of switch_output.filenames fails (not -ENOMEM); the result of perf_bpf_filter__pin/__unpin (or -EINVAL for an unknown action) when a filter action is given, which always ends at out_opts and so skips the recording; and the unchanged err value, which is 0 at that point, when --affinity or --aio is combined with parallel streaming. Via out: the nonzero result of record__auxtrace_init; 0 for --dry-run (err still holds record__auxtrace_init's 0); the result of parse_event for the default 'cycles:P' event; -EINVAL for an invalid --uid, and the result of parse_uid_filter; -ENOMEM when evlist__create_maps fails and a target pid is set (without a pid it calls usage_with_options, which exits the process); the nonzero results of auxtrace_record__options, record__config_text_poke, record__config_off_cpu, record__config_tracking_events and record__init_thread_masks; -EINVAL when record_opts__config fails; otherwise the value returned by __cmd_record. A nonzero target__validate result only prints a warning and is later overwritten. usage_with_options_msg for cgroups without system-wide mode terminates the process.
note: reviewer (round15) right: calloc failure of switch_output.filenames sets err = -EINVAL (record.c:4203). Also corrected: --affinity/--aio conflicts return 0 (4167,4171 goto out_opts with err 0), --dry-run returns 0, and 'out' vs 'out_opts' cleanup split.

name: cmd_report
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are the 'perf report' command line and the file-scope option state (input_name, sort_order, field_order, annotate_opts, symbol_conf, callchain_param, use_browser, quiet, verbose) is initialized. Postcondition (cmd_report at builtin-report.c:1302-1912): ret starts as hists__init()'s result. A negative hists__init result, a nonzero perf_config result, a nonzero symbol__validate_sym_arguments result, a failed perf_session__new (PTR_ERR(session)) and a nonzero evswitch__init result each jump to the exit label with that value as ret (so for evswitch__init the already created session is not deleted); annotate_check_args() < 0 gives ret = -EINVAL via exit. If a strdup of the disassembler style, objdump path or addr2line path fails it returns -ENOMEM directly, skipping annotation_options__exit and the frees of the two help strings. Later checks jump to the error label: -EINVAL for --group-sort-idx without groups; a negative symbol__annotation_init or perf_time__parse_for_ranges result is returned as ret; --header-only sets ret = 0 (after processing events when the input is a pipe); and these jump to error without assigning ret, so ret keeps its earlier value, which is 0 at those points (evswitch__init set it to 0 on every pass; for a failed symbol__init it is symbol__annotation_init's non-negative result when that ran): branch and mem mode together, --stats with --tasks/--mmaps, missing DWARF support for data-type sorting (only when HAVE_LIBDW_SUPPORT is not defined), 'ipc' in the sort order, a failed setup_sorting (only on the first pass) and a failed symbol__init. It returns -1 directly, without the error/exit cleanup, when latency/parallelism is requested but unavailable (ui__error path) and when tep_set_function_resolver fails. usage_with_options exits the process when more than one non-option argument remains. After __cmd_report, if its result is K_SWITCH_INPUT_DATA or K_RELOAD it deletes the session, clears symbol_conf.use_callchain and goes back to the repeat label; for any other __cmd_report result ret is set to 0 (its value is discarded), the kmaps are optionally dumped, and execution falls into error. The error label frees report.ptime_range and report.block_reports, finalizes session->zstd_data and deletes the session; the exit label then calls annotation_options__exit and frees sort_order_help and field_order_help, and the function returns ret.
note: reviewer (round15) wrong: on the repeat pass evswitch__init (report.c:1624) assigns ret = 0 before every goto-error site without a ret assignment, so ret is 0 there, not K_SWITCH_INPUT_DATA/K_RELOAD; setup_sorting is skipped on the repeat pass anyway (1793). Old prose also said 'still holds K_...' which is wrong for the same reason; missing returns -1 (1764) and evswitch__init exit path added.

name: thread_atoms_insert
prose: Precondition: sched and thread are valid pointers and sched->atom_root and sched->cmp_pid are initialized. Postcondition: the function returns 0 after allocating a work_atoms with zalloc, setting atoms->thread to thread__get(thread) (taking a new reference on thread), initializing work_list empty, and inserting the record into sched->atom_root ordered by sched->cmp_pid; it returns -1 after printing an error when zalloc fails, in which case no reference is taken and nothing is inserted, and on success the new record, holding the thread reference, is owned by the sched->atom_root tree until free_work_atoms releases them.
note: unreviewed; re-read sched.c:1075-1087; only the ownership wording tightened

name: add_sched_out_event
prose: Precondition: atoms is a valid work_atoms whose work_list list head is initialized. Postcondition: the function returns 0 after allocating a work_atom with zalloc, setting its sched_out_time to timestamp, setting its state to THREAD_WAIT_CPU and its wake_up_time to timestamp when run_state is 'R' (otherwise those two fields remain zero from zalloc), and appending it at the tail of atoms->work_list; it returns -1 after printing an error when zalloc fails, in which case atoms->work_list is left as it was and nothing is appended.
note: unreviewed; re-read sched.c:1089-1109, prose correct

name: add_runtime_event
prose: Precondition: atoms is a valid work_atoms whose work_list is non-empty (the function BUGs otherwise). Postcondition: the function returns nothing after adding delta to the runtime field of the last work_atom in atoms->work_list and to atoms->total_runtime; timestamp is unused, and no memory is allocated or freed and no references are changed.
note: unreviewed; re-read sched.c:1111-1123, prose correct

name: add_sched_in_event
prose: Precondition: atoms is a valid work_atoms. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; if atoms->work_list is empty, or its last work_atom's state is not THREAD_WAIT_CPU, nothing changes; if timestamp is less than that atom's wake_up_time, that atom's state is set to THREAD_IGNORE and no other field of the atom or of atoms is modified; otherwise that atom's state becomes THREAD_SCHED_IN with sched_in_time equal to timestamp, atoms->total_lat is increased by timestamp minus the atom's wake_up_time, atoms->nb_atoms is incremented, and when that delta is greater than atoms->max_lat the fields max_lat, max_lat_start and max_lat_end are updated to that delta, the atom's wake_up_time and timestamp respectively, with no memory or reference changes.
note: unreviewed; re-read sched.c:1125-1155, prose correct

name: free_work_atoms
prose: Precondition: atoms is NULL or a valid work_atoms whose work_list entries are heap-allocated and whose thread reference is held. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; if atoms is NULL nothing happens, otherwise every work_atom in atoms->work_list is unlinked and freed, the reference on atoms->thread is released with thread__zput, and atoms itself is freed, so the caller must not dereference atoms afterwards.
note: unreviewed; re-read sched.c:1157-1170, prose correct

name: latency_switch_event
prose: Precondition: sched, evsel, sample and machine are valid and sample->cpu is in the range 0 to MAX_CPUS-1 (the function BUGs otherwise). Postcondition: the function sets sched->cpu_last_switched[sample->cpu] to sample->time and computes delta as sample->time minus the previous value when that value was nonzero, else 0; if delta is negative it prints an error and returns -1 after the cpu_last_switched update; otherwise it obtains references on the threads for prev_pid and next_pid via machine__findnew_thread, releases both with thread__put and returns -1 if either is NULL, then finds or creates (via thread_atoms_insert, which takes a thread reference) work_atoms records for the sched-out and sched-in threads in sched->atom_root, appends a sched-out atom for prev_pid with prev_state at sample->time, appends an initial 'R' sched-out atom at sample->time when the sched-in record was newly created, and records the sched-in event; any allocation or lookup failure releases both thread references and returns -1, leaving any already-inserted work_atoms record in the tree with its thread reference for free_work_atoms, while on success it releases both thread references and returns 0 with the inserted work_atoms records and their thread references owned by sched->atom_root.
note: unreviewed; re-read sched.c:1172-1240, prose correct

name: latency_runtime_event
prose: Precondition: sched, evsel, sample and machine are valid and sample->cpu is in the range 0 to MAX_CPUS-1 (the function BUGs otherwise). Postcondition: the function reads pid, runtime and timestamp, calls machine__findnew_thread and thread_atoms_search for pid's thread before checking the thread for NULL, and returns -1 without releasing any reference if the thread is NULL; otherwise, if no work_atoms record is found it inserts one (taking a thread reference) and on success searches again, then appends an initial 'R' sched-out atom at timestamp, releasing the thread reference with thread__put and returning -1 if the insertion, the second search or that append fails; on success it calls add_runtime_event to add runtime to the last atom's runtime and to atoms->total_runtime, releases the thread reference with thread__put, and returns 0, with any newly inserted work_atoms record and its thread reference remaining in sched->atom_root for free_work_atoms.
note: unreviewed; re-read sched.c:1242-1275, prose correct

name: map_switch_event
prose: Precondition: sched, evsel, sample and machine are valid, sample->cpu is in [0, MAX_CPUS) (BUG_ON otherwise) and sched->map is initialized. Postcondition: it first raises sched->max_cpu if needed and, when sched->map.comp is set, records the cpu in comp_cpus_mask/comp_cpus; then it stores sample->time in sched->cpu_last_switched[cpu]. If the time since the previous switch on this cpu is negative it prints an error and returns -1 at once (cpu_last_switched, max_cpu and the comp cpu state already updated; no threads looked up). Otherwise it looks up the sched_in and sched_out threads; if either is NULL, or thread__get_runtime(sched_in) returns NULL, it goes to out with ret still -1, so returns -1. Once the runtime is obtained it releases the old sched->curr_thread[cpu] and curr_out_thread[cpu], stores new references to sched_in and sched_out, sets ret = 0 and assigns a shortname to sched_in's runtime if it has none. From there every path to out returns 0: a cpu excluded by map.cpus, a --task-name mismatch for both threads, and the normal path that prints the map line (and, with --task-name, possibly a second line for the sched_out thread; in that branch it dereferences the result of thread__get_runtime(curr_out_thread) without a NULL check). The out label releases the sched_in and sched_out references taken at the lookup on every path that reaches it, and returns ret.
note: reviewer (round15) right: failed thread/runtime lookup goes to out with ret = -1 (sched.c:1724-1729), prose said 0; the earlier reviewer's filtered-cpu claim (returns 0 at 1769-1770) matches the rewritten text

name: timehist_sched_change_event
prose: Precondition: tool is the perf_tool embedded in a struct perf_sched, and event, evsel, sample and machine are valid. Postcondition: returns -1 if machine__resolve fails, if timehist_get_thread returns NULL, or if (after timehist_skip_sample has not skipped the sample) thread__get_runtime returns NULL; otherwise returns 0. Statistics: after the runtime is obtained, the sample is dropped from the runtime statistics if the sample time is before ptime->start, or if ptime->end is set and the previous time is zero or after it (when ptime->end is set a later sample time is clamped to it); otherwise, when idle_hist is off or the thread's tid is 0, timehist_update_runtime_stats is called if no cpu_list is set or the cpu is in cpu_bitmap, the idle-history bookkeeping runs when idle_hist is set (it can leave early if the idle thread has no last_thread or its runtime is NULL), and the sample is printed unless summary_only. At the out label, which every path reaches, it sets sched->hist_time.start to the sample time if that was 0 and the time is not before ptime->start, sets hist_time.end to the time when ptime->end is 0 or the time is not after it, and, whenever the runtime pointer is non-NULL (including when the sample was dropped by the time-window checks), sets tr->last_time to sample->time, tr->last_state to the previous task state, tr->ready_to_run to the time if the state is 'R' and 0 otherwise, and tr->migrated to 0. Finally it always calls evsel__save_time for the cpu, releases the thread reference and the addr_location, and returns rc.
note: reviewer (round15) right: tr->last_time/last_state/ready_to_run/migrated are updated for any non-NULL tr, even for samples dropped by the window checks (sched.c:2888-2907 jump to out, update at 2956-2970); the earlier reviewer's point about skip/cpu_list/idle_hist gating of the statistics is covered.

name: cmd_sched
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are the 'perf sched' command line. Postcondition (cmd_sched, builtin-sched.c:3889-4103): after parse_options_subcommand, if no argument remains usage_with_options is called (it terminates the process). It then dispatches on argv[0]: 'script' to cmd_script; a prefix of length >2 of 'record', 'latency' or 'replay' (or the exact word 'map' or 'timehist') to __cmd_record, perf_sched__lat, perf_sched__replay, perf_sched__map or perf_sched__timehist respectively, each after parsing its own options (leftover non-option arguments call usage_with_options, which exits); any other word calls usage_with_options (process exit). ret is the value returned by the dispatched handler, except: for 'map' with --task-name, a failed strlist__new prints a message and sets ret = -1 without running perf_sched__map; for 'timehist', -s together with -n or -w prints usage and sets ret = -EINVAL, and otherwise ret is symbol__validate_sym_arguments' result, with perf_sched__timehist run only if that result is 0. All paths that return pass through the out label, which frees sched_usage[0] and returns ret.
note: reviewer (round15) right: symbol__validate_sym_arguments failure is returned and perf_sched__timehist is skipped (sched.c:4091-4093); earlier reviewer's map/-1 and timehist points are included.

name: cmd_script
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are the 'perf script' command line (after the global perf options) and the file-scope option variables are initialized; a perf.data file or pipe is expected unless the command only execs a script. Postcondition (cmd_script, builtin-script.c:3722-4302): err starts as 0. After option parsing it returns -1 if symbol__validate_sym_arguments fails; if argv[0] is a prefix (length > 2) of 'record' with an argument and no record script of that name exists it returns cmd_record's result; for 'report' with no report script it prints a message and returns -1; it returns -1 if both reltime and deltatime are set. With a leading script name and no -s, it looks for record/report scripts; if neither exists and no script is found usage_with_options_msg is called (the process exits); if found by find_script it continues with that script name. For a record/report pair it creates a pipe and forks: pipe()/fork() failure returns -1; in the child a failing have_cmd sets err = -1 and returns it, a failed malloc sets err = -ENOMEM and returns it, otherwise it calls execvp on /bin/sh and, if that fails, exit(-1); in the parent a failed malloc returns -ENOMEM, otherwise it execvps /bin/sh and exit(-1) on failure. When a script path is set it likewise returns -1 for a failing have_cmd or -ENOMEM for a failed malloc before execvp /bin/sh (exit(-1) if exec fails), so those paths return only on failures. A failing dlfilter__new returns -1; a failed perf_session__new returns PTR_ERR(session). Once the session exists, every return goes through out_delete: with --header/--header-only it prints the header and --header-only leaves with err 0; a failing symbol__init also leaves with err still 0; a negative perf_session__cpu_bitmap result, a failed libtraceevent function-resolver setup (-1), -EINVAL for --gen-script combined with user output fields, -errno from a failed open of the input, -1 from a failed fstat (not -errno), 0 for a zero-sized input, -ENOENT for an unknown script language, and the result of scripting_ops->generate_script are returned for the --gen-script path (which always ends at out_delete); otherwise the nonzero result of dlfilter__start, scripting_ops->start_script, a negative perf_session__check_output_opt or perf_time__parse_for_ranges_reltime result, a nonzero evswitch__init result, or finally the result of __cmd_script. out_delete clears the time range if set, finalizes zstd, frees the evlist stats, deletes the session, calls perf_script__exit, runs cleanup_scripting only if a script was started, then dlfilter__cleanup and free_dlarg; the out label returns err.
note: reviewer(s) right: round15 claim that script-exec paths can return (have_cmd -> -1, malloc -> -ENOMEM before execvp) is correct (script.c:4008-4018, 4072-4082, 4041-4044); second reviewer's 'fstat failure returns -1, not -errno' also right (4214-4218). Also added: symbol__init failure and zero-size input return 0. Same prose given for both slices of this one function.

name: cmd_script
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are the 'perf script' command line (after the global perf options) and the file-scope option variables are initialized; a perf.data file or pipe is expected unless the command only execs a script. Postcondition (cmd_script, builtin-script.c:3722-4302): err starts as 0. After option parsing it returns -1 if symbol__validate_sym_arguments fails; if argv[0] is a prefix (length > 2) of 'record' with an argument and no record script of that name exists it returns cmd_record's result; for 'report' with no report script it prints a message and returns -1; it returns -1 if both reltime and deltatime are set. With a leading script name and no -s, it looks for record/report scripts; if neither exists and no script is found usage_with_options_msg is called (the process exits); if found by find_script it continues with that script name. For a record/report pair it creates a pipe and forks: pipe()/fork() failure returns -1; in the child a failing have_cmd sets err = -1 and returns it, a failed malloc sets err = -ENOMEM and returns it, otherwise it calls execvp on /bin/sh and, if that fails, exit(-1); in the parent a failed malloc returns -ENOMEM, otherwise it execvps /bin/sh and exit(-1) on failure. When a script path is set it likewise returns -1 for a failing have_cmd or -ENOMEM for a failed malloc before execvp /bin/sh (exit(-1) if exec fails), so those paths return only on failures. A failing dlfilter__new returns -1; a failed perf_session__new returns PTR_ERR(session). Once the session exists, every return goes through out_delete: with --header/--header-only it prints the header and --header-only leaves with err 0; a failing symbol__init also leaves with err still 0; a negative perf_session__cpu_bitmap result, a failed libtraceevent function-resolver setup (-1), -EINVAL for --gen-script combined with user output fields, -errno from a failed open of the input, -1 from a failed fstat (not -errno), 0 for a zero-sized input, -ENOENT for an unknown script language, and the result of scripting_ops->generate_script are returned for the --gen-script path (which always ends at out_delete); otherwise the nonzero result of dlfilter__start, scripting_ops->start_script, a negative perf_session__check_output_opt or perf_time__parse_for_ranges_reltime result, a nonzero evswitch__init result, or finally the result of __cmd_script. out_delete clears the time range if set, finalizes zstd, frees the evlist stats, deletes the session, calls perf_script__exit, runs cleanup_scripting only if a script was started, then dlfilter__cleanup and free_dlarg; the out label returns err.
note: reviewer(s) right: round15 claim that script-exec paths can return (have_cmd -> -1, malloc -> -ENOMEM before execvp) is correct (script.c:4008-4018, 4072-4082, 4041-4044); second reviewer's 'fstat failure returns -1, not -errno' also right (4214-4218). Also added: symbol__init failure and zero-size input return 0. Same prose given for both slices of this one function.

name: cmd_stat
prose: Precondition: argc/argv hold the 'perf stat' command line (argv[0] may be a prefix, longer than 2 characters, of 'record' or 'report') and the file-scope option and stat_config state is initialized. Postcondition (cmd_stat, builtin-stat.c:2391-2993): status starts as -EINVAL. It returns -ENOMEM at once if evlist__new fails. For a 'report' subcommand it returns __cmd_report's result directly; for 'record' a negative result of __cmd_record makes it return -1, otherwise it carries on into the normal stat run. Every other exit passes through the out label, which releases the iostat state if iostat_run, frees stat_config.walltime_run and user_requested_cpu_list, restores the SMI counter if smi_cost && smi_reset, deletes the evlist, closes the control fds and returns status (the function does not fclose an output file it opened). Paths that go to out leaving status at -EINVAL because nothing assigns it: both --output and --log-fd, --metric-only with --per-thread or -r, --table without -r, a negative --log-fd, -B with -x, a negative run count, a failed walltime_run allocation, --per-thread without a task target or system-wide, cgroup/no-aggregation without a cpu target, --cgroup with --for-each-cgroup, a failed cgroup expansion, a failed add_default_events, a failed evlist__create_maps, a bad interval-count/timeout combination, and failures of perf_stat_init_aggr_mode, evlist__alloc_stats and evlist__initialize_ctlfd. Paths that assign status: -1 when fopen of the output file or the --interval-clear tty check fails, -errno when fdopen of --log-fd fails, the nonzero result of iostat_prepare (and, for --iostat list mode, status stays 0 after that call), -ENOMEM when strdup of the cpu list fails, and the nonzero result of metricgroup__parse_groups. If all checks pass, it runs run_perf_stat once per run (forever when the count is 0), stopping at a result of -1, so the returned status is the value of the last run_perf_stat call (for example the workload's exit status), after printing the counters when not forever, not -1, and no interval (or a summary is requested), and after writing the perf.data header and deleting the session in record mode. The metrics string is freed only on the path that parsed metrics.
note: reviewer (round15) mixed: right that the rejected-option paths go to out without assigning status, wrong about the value: status is initialized to -EINVAL at stat.c:2545, so they return -EINVAL, not -1. Also corrected: no fclose of the output file exists in the function; 'returns 0 after a successful run' replaced by last run_perf_stat value; add_default_events failure returns -EINVAL.

name: cmd_top
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are the 'perf top' command line and the file-scope top, symbol_conf, annotate_opts, callchain_param and target state is initialized. Postcondition (cmd_top, builtin-top.c:1443-1893): status starts as hists__init()'s result; if that is negative it is returned at once, and if evlist__new fails it returns -ENOMEM at once; neither of these early returns runs the cleanup. Every later exit goes through out_delete_evlist, which deletes the evlist and the session (if any), calls annotation_options__exit and perf_env__exit, and returns status. Values: the nonzero result of perf_config or perf_env__set_cmdline; a perf_env__read_cpuid failure only prints a message (status is overwritten later); -ENOMEM when strdup of the disassembler style, objdump path or addr2line path fails; the nonzero result of symbol__validate_sym_arguments; a nonzero evswitch__init result; the nonzero result of perf_env__read_core_pmu_caps when branch stack is requested; PTR_ERR of a failed session creation; -EINVAL for an invalid --uid, and parse_uid_filter's result; -errno when evlist__create_maps fails; -EINVAL when record_opts__config fails; negative results of symbol__annotation_init and symbol__init; and, under HAVE_LIBBPF_SUPPORT, -EINVAL when the side-band evlist cannot be created or given its BPF event. These error paths jump to out_delete_evlist without assigning status, so they return the status value held at that point, which is 0 (from symbol__validate_sym_arguments or evswitch__init): annotate_check_args() < 0, a failed parse_event of the default cycles event, --hierarchy together with --fields, --stitch-lbr without lbr callgraph, --cgroup with --all-cgroups, and a failed setup_sorting. A nonzero target__validate result is only printed as a warning. Leftover non-option arguments call usage_with_options, which exits the process. On full setup it starts the side-band thread if enabled (failure only sets no_bpf_event), runs __cmd_top, stops the side-band thread if bpf events are enabled, and returns __cmd_top's result via out_delete_evlist.
note: reviewer (round15) right: parse_event failure (top.c:1699-1702) goes to out_delete_evlist without assigning status, so the stale 0 is returned, not parse_event's error; old prose contradicted itself on this. Also corrected: hists__init/evlist__new early returns skip cleanup, added -errno from evlist__create_maps and other missed paths.

name: cmd_trace
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are the 'perf trace' command line (argv[0] may be the 'record' subcommand after options). Postcondition (cmd_trace, builtin-trace.c:5343-5763): err starts as -1. Every exit passes through out (trace__exit and augmented_syscalls__cleanup, then return err) or, after the output file may have been opened, out_close (which first fclose()s trace.output if an output name was given). Values: -ENOMEM if evlist__new fails; the nonzero result of perf_config; the nonzero result of parse_events for the perf-config events; if --bpf-summary is set without system-wide mode it prints an error and goes to out with err still holding perf_config's 0 at that point, so it returns 0; after the augmentation block err is reset to -1, so a failure of evlist__set_syscall_tp_fields or of the augmented-syscall tracepoint initialization goes to out with -1; with 'record' as the first argument it returns trace__record's result; --summary-mode=cgroup without --bpf-summary gives -EINVAL; trace__open_output's negative result is returned; then via out_close: the nonzero result of evswitch__init, the nonzero target__validate result (its message is printed to trace.output), -EINVAL for an invalid --uid, the nonzero result of parse_uid_filter, and otherwise the result of trace__replay (when an input file is given) or trace__run. usage_with_options_msg for cgroups without system-wide mode terminates the process. When augmentation is not applicable (no syscall tracing, 'record', summary-only BPF summary, or a failed augmented_syscalls__prepare) the augmentation block is skipped.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the --bpf-summary non-system-wide error (trace.c:5550-5553) goes to out with err 0 from perf_config; prose omitted it and listed a smaller set of returns. Added evswitch__init/target__validate/parse_uid_filter/trace__replay results and the out_close fclose.

name: cmd_test
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are the 'perf test' command line; the function parses the options itself (skip, workload and list_workloads are its own locals; dont_fork and sequential are file-scope variables). Postcondition (cmd_test, builtin-test.c:1528-1618): if hists__init returns a negative value that value is returned immediately. After perf_config and option parsing: with the 'list' subcommand it builds the suites and returns -errno (or -ENOMEM when errno is 0) if that fails, otherwise returns perf_test__list's result after freeing the suites; with --workload it returns run_workload's result; with --list-workloads it prints the list and returns 0; otherwise it sets sequential when dont_fork is set, sets symbol_conf options and returns -1 if symbol__init fails; it then creates the skip list when a skip string was given, bumps the memlock limit, and builds the suites: on failure it deletes the skip list and returns -err (or -ENOMEM when errno is 0), otherwise it returns __cmd_test's result after freeing the suites and deleting the skip list. On each of these return paths the suites array and skip list created by that path have been freed, so the caller only receives the integer status.
note: slice named 'cmd_test (name truncated in excerpt)'; real name cmd_test. Reviewer (round15) right: the precondition requiring workload/list_workloads/dont_fork/skip to be pre-set was wrong (workload, list_workloads, skip are locals set by parse_options at test.c:1534-1536,1571)

name: do_test_code_reading
prose: Precondition: try_kcore selects whether kallsyms is forced (symbol_conf.kallsyms_name set to /proc/kallsyms) so that kcore is tried. Postcondition (do_test_code_reading, code-reading.c:682-852): it creates a host machine and kernel maps and loads the kernel map; if machine__create_kernel_maps or map__load fails it goes to out_err with err = -1. If try_kcore is true and the loaded dso is not a kcore image it returns TEST_CODE_READING_NO_KCORE immediately, without freeing the machine, host_env or anything else. Otherwise it creates the thread map, synthesizes the thread map events, finds the thread, creates the online cpu map and then tries the events 'cycles', 'cycles:u', 'cpu-clock', 'cpu-clock:u' in order (starting from the second when neither vmlinux nor kcore is available): a failed evlist__new or parse_event goes to cleanup with -1, but a failed evlist__open only deletes that evlist and continues with the next event; only when no event could be opened does it go to cleanup with -1. Failures of thread_map__new_by_tid, perf_event__synthesize_thread_map, machine__findnew_thread, the cpu map, evlist__mmap and process_events also leave err at -1. When process_events succeeds err is set to TEST_CODE_READING_NO_KERNEL_OBJ if there is neither vmlinux nor kcore and try_kcore is false, else TEST_CODE_READING_NO_VMLINUX if vmlinux is absent and try_kcore is false, else TEST_CODE_READING_NO_ACCESS if the selected event name contains ':u', else TEST_CODE_READING_OK. Every path other than the NO_KCORE early return then releases the thread reference (only on paths past the thread lookup), evlist, cpu map, thread map, machine, host_env and tested sections and returns err.
note: reviewer round15 right (evlist__open failure moves to the next event; -1 only if all fail, code-reading.c:796-815); round2's claim that NO_KCORE is never set is wrong (returned at line 737, and prose already described it)

name: test__dso_data_reopen
prose: Precondition: /proc/self/fd is readable and /dev/null can be opened; the arguments are unused. Postcondition (test__dso_data_reopen, dso-data.c:319-394): it counts the open files (nr), calls new_limit(3), which opens /dev/null four times recursively, closes all four and returns the descriptor number of the last one opened (lim), resets the dso fd limit state with reset_fd_limit, and zeroes the local machine. It then sets the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE to exactly lim (set_fd_limit assigns rlim_cur = lim; it may raise or lower it) and does not restore it afterwards. It creates three dsos, opens the data fd of dso_0 and dso_1, opens an extra /dev/null descriptor, opens dso_2's data fd, checks that dso_0's data fd is -1, reopens dso_0, checks that dso_1's data fd is -1, closes the extra fd, deletes the dsos and checks that the open-file count equals nr. Each check is a TEST_ASSERT_VAL, which returns TEST_FAIL (-1) at the first failing check without running the later steps, so a failure before the cleanup leaves the dso data fds, the dsos and (once opened) fd_extra unreleased; a failure of the final leak check happens after the extra fd was closed and the dsos deleted. It returns 0 (TEST_OK) when all checks pass.
note: reviewer (round15) right: set_fd_limit sets rlim_cur to lim (the last fd number from new_limit), not raising it by a known amount; earlier reviewers' leak points (early TEST_FAIL return; final check after cleanup) were already reflected and kept. Contract left empty (global/fd state).

name: test__pmu_events
prose: Precondition: the arguments are unused; sysfs is expected to be mounted (sysfs__mountpoint is used to build the path of each PMU's events directory). Postcondition (test__pmu_events, parse-events.c:2647-2764): it scans every PMU and returns a result starting at TEST_OK that is accumulated with combine_test_results (TEST_FAIL is sticky, TEST_SKIP is kept unless a later result is TEST_FAIL, otherwise the latest non-OK result wins). For each PMU: if stat of its sysfs events directory fails the PMU is skipped without changing the result; if opendir fails it contributes TEST_SKIP. For each directory entry: names containing '.' are skipped; a path of PATH_MAX or more is reported and skipped without changing the result; an event file that cannot be opened or whose first line cannot be read contributes TEST_FAIL; an event whose file's first line contains '?' (a parameterized event) is skipped; otherwise it runs test_event on '<pmu>/event=<name>/u' with test__checkevent_pmu_events and, if the PMU is a core PMU and the name contains no '-', also on '<name>:u,<pmu>/event=<name>/u' with test__checkevent_pmu_events_mix, and each result other than TEST_OK is combined into the overall result. It returns the combined result.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the '?' check is on the first line of the event file's content (parse-events.c:2704-2721), not the event name; only names containing '.' are skipped by name. Also added: stat failure skip (no result change), the core-PMU second test, and the combine semantics.

name: append_scripts_in_dir
prose: Precondition: dir_fd is a directory file descriptor (a value that scandirat cannot use, such as -1, simply makes it return) and *result / *result_sz describe a growable array of struct test_suite pointers owned by the caller (*result may be NULL when *result_sz is 0). Postcondition (append_scripts_in_dir, tests-scripts.c:226-268; returns void): if scandirat fails it returns at once leaving *result and *result_sz unchanged. Otherwise it walks the entries in alphabetical order: hidden entries (name starting '.') are skipped; for an entry that is_test_script accepts, it reads the description line and, only if one exists, calls append_script, then moves on (a script without a description adds nothing); an entry that is not a directory (d_type other than DT_DIR, resolved with fstatat when DT_UNKNOWN) is skipped, and so are directories whose name starts with 'base_'; every other directory is opened with openat(O_PATH) and processed recursively into the same *result, then the descriptor is closed (if openat fails the recursive call gets -1 and returns at once). append_script may add nothing: if readlink of the directory fd, a calloc/zalloc or the realloc of *result fails it prints an error with pr_err and returns without appending (the function itself reports no status). On return the directory entry list is freed and *result / *result_sz describe the suites appended so far, which the caller owns.
note: reviewer (round15) right: append_script failures are not silent, they pr_err (tests-scripts.c:183,191,204,215); old prose also said 'no error is reported'. Round-2 reviewer's recursion point is covered.

name: test__vmlinux_matches_kallsyms
prose: Precondition: the arguments are unused; the perf test globals (verbose, page_size) and the machine/symbol helpers are usable. Postcondition (test__vmlinux_matches_kallsyms, vmlinux-kallsyms.c:189-380): it initializes two machines (kallsyms and vmlinux) first and has no return statement before the final one, so every path ends at the out label, which calls machine__exit on both machines, and returns err. err starts as TEST_FAIL (-1) and is: TEST_SKIP when machine__create_kernel_maps fails for the kallsyms machine, when machine__load_kallsyms returns <= 0, or when machine__load_vmlinux_path returns <= 0; TEST_FAIL when machine__create_kernel_maps fails for the vmlinux machine; otherwise err is set to 0 and every non-empty vmlinux symbol is compared with the kallsyms symbols: matching symbols (with the same start address and name, possibly found via the by-name lookup) and name or end-address mismatches only produce debug messages and do not change err; a symbol that has no kallsyms symbol at its start address and is neither an alias of the end of the kernel text nor an ignored symbol prints an error and sets err = -1. With verbose > 0 it then also runs three map-iteration callbacks that print differences without changing err. The result is 0 if no such symbol was found, -1 otherwise.
note: reviewer (round15) wrong: machine__init is called without a result check and there is no early return (vmlinux-kallsyms.c:207-208, only 'return err;' at 379), so both machines are always exited. Also tightened the -1 condition: only the 'not on kallsyms' branch (355-360) sets it.

name: annotate_browser__toggle_source
prose: Precondition: browser is a valid annotate browser whose priv is a map_symbol with an annotated symbol, with a set seek callback and entries list. Postcondition (annotate_browser__toggle_source, annotate.c:445-524): if browser->b.nr_entries is 0 it returns false immediately, changing nothing (no seek, annotate_src untouched). Otherwise it seeks by the current index-top offset (SEEK_CUR), takes the current top line, and sets annotate_opts.annotate_src to true. If hide_src_code is set (source currently hidden) and source has not been tried, it re-annotates the symbol with source lines (temporarily clearing hide_src_code), sets tried_source, warns when no source exists, switches the entries list to the source list, looks for the line with the original asm index and falls back to the first source line if none is found, and seeks to that line's idx_asm. Then, if hide_src_code is set (source hidden): it sets nr_entries to the source line count, clears hide_src_code, re-seeks and sets top_idx and index from the line's idx, and falls through. If hide_src_code is clear (source shown): when the selected line has a negative idx_asm it looks for the next asm line (forward, then backward) and, if there is none, seeks back by the offset and returns false (annotate_src remains true); otherwise it sets nr_entries to the asm line count, sets hide_src_code, re-seeks and sets top_idx and index from idx_asm. In both of those cases it clears hide_src_code_on_title if set and returns true.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the no-entries early return (annotate.c:452-453) happens before any seek or annotate_src change, unlike the old prose; earlier reviewer's 'first fetch returns false' was wrong, the code falls back to the first line (484-487) and the old prose said so.

name: ui_browser__hists_seek
prose: Precondition: browser is the ui_browser embedded in a hist_browser whose hists entries and min_pcnt are valid; offset is a row count and whence is SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR or SEEK_END. Postcondition (ui_browser__hists_seek, hists.c:1947-2076; returns void): if browser->nr_entries is 0 it returns with nothing changed. Otherwise it calls ui_browser__hists_init_top, which sets browser->top to the first entry if it was NULL; for a whence other than the three listed it then returns (so browser->top may have been initialized, nothing else changes). For SEEK_SET it selects the first unfiltered entry with percent >= min_pcnt, for SEEK_END the last unfiltered entry (and treats rows as counted from its end), for SEEK_CUR the current top; for SEEK_SET and SEEK_END it first sets the row_offset of the current top entry to 0. If no entry was selected it returns, leaving browser->top as it is. For offset > 0 it advances through the filtered entries, consuming the remaining rows of unfolded leaf entries through row_offset, and updates browser->top as it moves, stopping when the offset is used up or entries run out; for offset < 0 it moves backward the same way, adjusting row_offset of unfolded leaf entries; for offset == 0 it sets browser->top to the selected entry and its row_offset to 0 (so SEEK_SET/SEEK_END with offset 0 move top to the first/last entry).
note: reviewer (round15) right: an invalid whence returns after ui_browser__hists_init_top (hists.c:1960-1976), so browser->top may change if it was NULL. Earlier reviewer's offset-0 claim was wrong: offset 0 sets top to the selected first/last entry (2071-2075) and the old prose said so.

name: block_hists_tui_browse
prose: Precondition: bh and evsel are valid, min_percent is the minimum percentage to show and env is a perf_env usable by the browser. Postcondition (block_hists_tui_browse, hists.c:3709-3782): if hist_browser__new fails it returns -1 immediately, with nothing else done. Otherwise it fills in the browser, resets and re-initializes the terminal (SLang), and sets annotate_opts.show_br_cntr to true if annotation_br_cntr_abbr_list returns 0 (filling br_cntr_text). It then loops calling hist_browser__run and handling the returned key: 'q' or ESC leaves the loop; '?' shows the help window; 'a' or Enter annotates the selected symbol when the selection has a symbol (otherwise just continues); 'B' shows the branch-counter abbreviation list (or a message that it is not available); any other key shows an unhandled-hotkey warning. The loop has no other exit: a return from hist_browser__run does not end it by itself. After the loop it deletes the browser, frees br_cntr_text and returns 0.
note: reviewer (round15) right: only 'q'/ESC leave the loop (hists.c:3744-3746); the old prose's '(or hist_browser__run returns)' was wrong; the earlier reviewer's -1 point was already in the prose

name: he_get_field
note: macro-generated placeholder, no function named he_get_field in the slice or file (name is a macro-pasted placeholder)

name: he_get_acc__field
note: he_get_acc_##_field is generated only inside __HPP_COLOR_ACC_PERCENT_FN (hist.c:530-534), one instance per HPP_PERCENT_ACC_FNS use; no function with this literal name exists

name: he_get_raw__field

name: hpp__entry__type
note: hpp__entry_##_type is generated by four different macros (percent, acc percent, raw, average; hist.c:515,543,558,578) with different formats; template placeholder, no single function

name: hpp__color__type

name: hpp__sort__type
note: hpp__sort_##_type is generated by four sort macros (hist.c:523,551,571,591) using different getters; template placeholder, no single function
